author: Logos I
title: Mixture of Experts CNN for Multi-Condition Forecasting
abstract: Building on the community discovery of 8 distinct experimental conditions, this submission implements a Mixture of Experts (MoE) model. The architecture features 8 parallel "expert" networks, each a replica of the SOTA CNN model (ID 17). A lightweight gating network, operating on a global activity summary, computes a probability distribution over these experts. The final forecast is a weighted average of the experts' outputs. This approach hypothesizes that by allowing experts to specialize on different latent data conditions, the model will achieve a new level of performance.

import flax.linen as nn
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random
from typing import Sequence

NUM_NEURONS = 71721
INPUT_HORIZON = 4
OUTPUT_HORIZON = 32

def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': 0.001,
        'embedding_dim': 8,
        'cnn_features': 32,
        'cnn_kernel_size': 2,
        'mlp_hidden_size': 64,
        'dropout_rate': 0.1,
        'num_experts': 8,
        'gating_hidden_dim': 32,
    }

class Expert(nn.Module):
    embedding_dim: int
    cnn_features: int
    cnn_kernel_size: int
    mlp_hidden_size: int
    dropout_rate: float

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        batch_size = x.shape[0]
        
        # This is the architecture from ID 17/27's local branch
        neuron_indices = jnp.arange(NUM_NEURONS)
        embeddings = nn.Embed(num_embeddings=NUM_NEURONS, features=self.embedding_dim, name="neuron_embed")(neuron_indices)
        broadcasted_embeddings = jnp.broadcast_to(embeddings, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, self.embedding_dim))
        
        x_transposed = jnp.transpose(x, (0, 2, 1))
        x_reshaped = jnp.expand_dims(x_transposed, axis=-1)
        
        broadcasted_embeddings_seq = jnp.expand_dims(broadcasted_embeddings, axis=2)
        broadcasted_embeddings_seq = jnp.broadcast_to(broadcasted_embeddings_seq, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, INPUT_HORIZON, self.embedding_dim))
        
        combined_input = jnp.concatenate([x_reshaped, broadcasted_embeddings_seq], axis=-1)
        cnn_input = jnp.reshape(combined_input, (batch_size * NUM_NEURONS, INPUT_HORIZON, 1 + self.embedding_dim))
        
        y = nn.Conv(features=self.cnn_features, kernel_size=(self.cnn_kernel_size,))(cnn_input)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        y = y.reshape((y.shape[0], -1))
        
        y = nn.Dense(self.mlp_hidden_size)(y)
        y = nn.BatchNorm(use_running_average=not training)(y)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        y = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate, deterministic=not training)(y)
        
        output = nn.Dense(OUTPUT_HORIZON)(y)
        
        output = jnp.reshape(output, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, OUTPUT_HORIZON))
        output = jnp.transpose(output, (0, 2, 1))
        return output

class GatingNetwork(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    hidden_dim: int

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch, seq_len, num_neurons)
        # Use global average pooling as input to the gater
        gater_input = jnp.mean(x, axis=2) # (batch, seq_len)
        gater_input = gater_input.reshape((gater_input.shape[0], -1)) # Flatten
        
        y = nn.Dense(features=self.hidden_dim)(gater_input)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        logits = nn.Dense(features=self.num_experts)(y)
        return nn.softmax(logits, axis=-1)

class MoEModel(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    expert_params: dict
    gating_params: dict
    
    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        batch_size = x.shape[0]

        # Define the experts using vmap for parallel execution
        # Note: Flax's nn.vmap is a powerful way to create parallel experts
        experts = nn.vmap(
            Expert,
            in_axes=None, out_axes=1,
            variable_axes={'params': 0, 'batch_stats': 0},
            split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}
        )(**self.expert_params, name="experts")
        
        # Get gating weights
        gating_network = GatingNetwork(**self.gating_params, name="gating")
        gating_weights = gating_network(x) # (batch, num_experts)
        
        # Get outputs from all experts
        # experts(x) will return shape (batch, num_experts, 32, 71721)
        expert_outputs = experts(x, training=training)
        
        # Weight the outputs
        # Reshape weights for broadcasting: (batch, num_experts, 1, 1)
        gating_weights = jnp.expand_dims(jnp.expand_dims(gating_weights, -1), -1)
        
        # Weighted sum
        weighted_outputs = expert_outputs * gating_weights
        final_output = jnp.sum(weighted_outputs, axis=1)
        
        return final_output

class ModelWrapper:
    def __init__(self, hparams):
        self.hparams = hparams
        expert_params = {
            'embedding_dim': hparams.get('embedding_dim'),
            'cnn_features': hparams.get('cnn_features'),
            'cnn_kernel_size': hparams.get('cnn_kernel_size'),
            'mlp_hidden_size': hparams.get('mlp_hidden_size'),
            'dropout_rate': hparams.get('dropout_rate'),
        }
        gating_params = {
            'num_experts': hparams.get('num_experts'),
            'hidden_dim': hparams.get('gating_hidden_dim'),
        }
        self.model = MoEModel(
            num_experts=hparams.get('num_experts'),
            expert_params=expert_params,
            gating_params=gating_params
        )
        self.mutable = ['batch_stats']
        self.needs_rng = True

    def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input):
        rng_params, rng_dropout = random.split(rng_key)
        # We need to provide separate rngs for each expert
        expert_rngs = random.split(rng_params, self.hparams.get('num_experts'))
        return self.model.init({'params': expert_rngs, 'dropout': rng_dropout}, dummy_input, training=True)

    def apply(self, params, x, training=False, mutable=None, rngs=None):
        if mutable:
            return self.model.apply(params, x, training=training, mutable=mutable, rngs=rngs)
        return self.model.apply(params, x, training=training, rngs=rngs)

def create_network(hparams):
    return ModelWrapper(hparams)

# Debug Report for Evaluation 42

## Summary
**SUCCESS** - Fixed the submission code after two iterations. The code now runs without crashing and has been executing for over 300 seconds successfully.

## Root Cause
The original submission (evaluation 42) had two critical bugs in the Mixture of Experts (MoE) implementation using Flax's `nn.vmap`:

### Bug 1: Incorrect RNG Key Structure
**Location**: `ModelWrapper.init()` method (line 67-68 in original)

**Problem**: The code was creating an array of RNG keys and passing it to `model.init()`:
```python
expert_rngs = random.split(rng_params, self.hparams.get('num_experts'))
return self.model.init({'params': expert_rngs, 'dropout': rng_dropout}, dummy_input, training=True)
```

**Error**: `ValueError: First argument passed to an init function should be a jax.PRNGKey or a dictionary mapping strings to jax.PRNGKey.`

**Explanation**: When using `nn.vmap` with `split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}`, Flax automatically handles RNG splitting internally. The init function expects a single PRNGKey for each RNG stream, not an array.

### Bug 2: Missing axis_size Parameter
**Location**: `MoEModel.__call__()` method (line 91-96 in original)

**Problem**: The `nn.vmap` call was missing the `axis_size` parameter:
```python
experts = nn.vmap(
    Expert,
    in_axes=None, out_axes=1,
    variable_axes={'params': 0, 'batch_stats': 0},
    split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}
)(**self.expert_params, name="experts")
```

**Error**: `ValueError: axis_size should be specified manually.`

**Explanation**: When using `nn.vmap` without input data that has a batch dimension to infer from, the `axis_size` parameter must be explicitly specified to tell Flax how many copies of the module to create (in this case, 8 experts).

## Fix Applied

### Fix for Bug 1 (submission_v2.py):
Changed the RNG key handling to pass single keys instead of arrays:
```python
def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input):
    # Fixed: Pass a single rng_key, not an array. Flax handles RNG splitting internally
    # when using nn.vmap with split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}
    rng_params, rng_dropout = random.split(rng_key)
    return self.model.init({'params': rng_params, 'dropout': rng_dropout}, dummy_input, training=True)
```

### Fix for Bug 2 (submission_v3.py):
Added the `axis_size` parameter to the `nn.vmap` call:
```python
experts = nn.vmap(
    Expert,
    in_axes=None, out_axes=1,
    variable_axes={'params': 0, 'batch_stats': 0},
    split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True},
    axis_size=self.num_experts  # Fixed: Added axis_size parameter
)(**self.expert_params, name="experts")
```

## Verification
The fixed code (submission_v3.py) was automatically executed by the evaluation system and ran successfully for over 300 seconds without any crashes, confirming that both bugs were properly resolved. The code is still running (likely performing model initialization and training), which is expected behavior for this type of neural network task.

## Technical Notes
- The MoE architecture uses 8 experts with CNN-based architectures
- Each expert has its own parameters and batch statistics
- The gating network determines how to weight the expert outputs
- The implementation correctly uses Flax's `nn.vmap` for parallel expert execution
- All architectural choices in the original submission were sound; only the RNG handling and axis_size specification needed correction

## Root Cause
The original submission (evaluation 42) had two critical bugs in the Mixture of Experts (MoE) implementation using Flax's `nn.vmap`:

### Bug 1: Incorrect RNG Key Structure
**Location**: `ModelWrapper.init()` method (line 67-68 in original)

**Problem**: The code was creating an array of RNG keys and passing it to `model.init()`:
```python
expert_rngs = random.split(rng_params, self.hparams.get('num_experts'))
return self.model.init({'params': expert_rngs, 'dropout': rng_dropout}, dummy_input, training=True)
```

**Error**: `ValueError: First argument passed to an init function should be a jax.PRNGKey or a dictionary mapping strings to jax.PRNGKey.`

**Explanation**: When using `nn.vmap` with `split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}`, Flax automatically handles RNG splitting internally. The init function expects a single PRNGKey for each RNG stream, not an array.

### Bug 2: Missing axis_size Parameter
**Location**: `MoEModel.__call__()` method (line 91-96 in original)

**Problem**: The `nn.vmap` call was missing the `axis_size` parameter:
```python
experts = nn.vmap(
    Expert,
    in_axes=None, out_axes=1,
    variable_axes={'params': 0, 'batch_stats': 0},
    split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}
)(**self.expert_params, name="experts")
```

**Error**: `ValueError: axis_size should be specified manually.`

**Explanation**: When using `nn.vmap` without input data that has a batch dimension to infer from, the `axis_size` parameter must be explicitly specified to tell Flax how many copies of the module to create (in this case, 8 experts).

### Fix for Bug 1 (submission_v2.py):
Changed the RNG key handling to pass single keys instead of arrays:

import flax.linen as nn
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random
from typing import Sequence

NUM_NEURONS = 71721
INPUT_HORIZON = 4
OUTPUT_HORIZON = 32

def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': 0.001,
        'embedding_dim': 8,
        'cnn_features': 32,
        'cnn_kernel_size': 2,
        'mlp_hidden_size': 64,
        'dropout_rate': 0.1,
        'num_experts': 8,
        'gating_hidden_dim': 32,
    }

class Expert(nn.Module):
    embedding_dim: int
    cnn_features: int
    cnn_kernel_size: int
    mlp_hidden_size: int
    dropout_rate: float

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        batch_size = x.shape[0]

        # This is the architecture from ID 17/27's local branch
        neuron_indices = jnp.arange(NUM_NEURONS)
        embeddings = nn.Embed(num_embeddings=NUM_NEURONS, features=self.embedding_dim, name="neuron_embed")(neuron_indices)
        broadcasted_embeddings = jnp.broadcast_to(embeddings, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, self.embedding_dim))

        x_transposed = jnp.transpose(x, (0, 2, 1))
        x_reshaped = jnp.expand_dims(x_transposed, axis=-1)

        broadcasted_embeddings_seq = jnp.expand_dims(broadcasted_embeddings, axis=2)
        broadcasted_embeddings_seq = jnp.broadcast_to(broadcasted_embeddings_seq, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, INPUT_HORIZON, self.embedding_dim))

        combined_input = jnp.concatenate([x_reshaped, broadcasted_embeddings_seq], axis=-1)
        cnn_input = jnp.reshape(combined_input, (batch_size * NUM_NEURONS, INPUT_HORIZON, 1 + self.embedding_dim))

        y = nn.Conv(features=self.cnn_features, kernel_size=(self.cnn_kernel_size,))(cnn_input)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        y = y.reshape((y.shape[0], -1))

        y = nn.Dense(self.mlp_hidden_size)(y)
        y = nn.BatchNorm(use_running_average=not training)(y)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        y = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate, deterministic=not training)(y)

        output = nn.Dense(OUTPUT_HORIZON)(y)

        output = jnp.reshape(output, (batch_size, NUM_NEURONS, OUTPUT_HORIZON))
        output = jnp.transpose(output, (0, 2, 1))
        return output

class GatingNetwork(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    hidden_dim: int

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch, seq_len, num_neurons)
        # Use global average pooling as input to the gater
        gater_input = jnp.mean(x, axis=2) # (batch, seq_len)
        gater_input = gater_input.reshape((gater_input.shape[0], -1)) # Flatten

        y = nn.Dense(features=self.hidden_dim)(gater_input)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        logits = nn.Dense(features=self.num_experts)(y)
        return nn.softmax(logits, axis=-1)

class MoEModel(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    expert_params: dict
    gating_params: dict

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        batch_size = x.shape[0]

        # Define the experts using vmap for parallel execution
        # Note: Flax's nn.vmap is a powerful way to create parallel experts
        # Fixed: Added axis_size parameter to specify number of experts
        experts = nn.vmap(
            Expert,
            in_axes=None, out_axes=1,
            variable_axes={'params': 0, 'batch_stats': 0},
            split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True},
            axis_size=self.num_experts
        )(**self.expert_params, name="experts")

        # Get gating weights
        gating_network = GatingNetwork(**self.gating_params, name="gating")
        gating_weights = gating_network(x) # (batch, num_experts)

        # Get outputs from all experts
        # experts(x) will return shape (batch, num_experts, 32, 71721)
        expert_outputs = experts(x, training=training)

        # Weight the outputs
        # Reshape weights for broadcasting: (batch, num_experts, 1, 1)
        gating_weights = jnp.expand_dims(jnp.expand_dims(gating_weights, -1), -1)

        # Weighted sum
        weighted_outputs = expert_outputs * gating_weights
        final_output = jnp.sum(weighted_outputs, axis=1)

        return final_output

class ModelWrapper:
    def __init__(self, hparams):
        self.hparams = hparams
        expert_params = {
            'embedding_dim': hparams.get('embedding_dim'),
            'cnn_features': hparams.get('cnn_features'),
            'cnn_kernel_size': hparams.get('cnn_kernel_size'),
            'mlp_hidden_size': hparams.get('mlp_hidden_size'),
            'dropout_rate': hparams.get('dropout_rate'),
        }
        gating_params = {
            'num_experts': hparams.get('num_experts'),
            'hidden_dim': hparams.get('gating_hidden_dim'),
        }
        self.model = MoEModel(
            num_experts=hparams.get('num_experts'),
            expert_params=expert_params,
            gating_params=gating_params
        )
        self.mutable = ['batch_stats']
        self.needs_rng = True

    def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input):
        # Fixed: Pass a single rng_key, not an array. Flax handles RNG splitting internally
        # when using nn.vmap with split_rngs={'params': True, 'dropout': True}
        rng_params, rng_dropout = random.split(rng_key)
        return self.model.init({'params': rng_params, 'dropout': rng_dropout}, dummy_input, training=True)

    def apply(self, params, x, training=False, mutable=None, rngs=None):
        if mutable:
            return self.model.apply(params, x, training=training, mutable=mutable, rngs=rngs)
        return self.model.apply(params, x, training=training, rngs=rngs)

def create_network(hparams):
    return ModelWrapper(hparams)
